rationale: C18 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both memoranda describe a private bill compensating a government contractor for losses on particular fixed-price work, then defeat the claim by comparing those losses with profits earned on the overall contract or broader government business. Both conclude that relief would improperly make the Government underwrite contractor losses and would discriminate against other contractors. C01 and C24 share the broader risk-allocation argument, but C18 has the closest factual analysis, operative sequence, and language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The record indicates that the Company made a net profit of over $64,000 on the thirty-five Government contracts ... despite the fact that as to seven of them it sustained losses.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Despite this loss of $29,432.29 on this contract ... the contractor actually earned a profit of $34,202.86 on the entire contract. The Audit report also discloses that this contractor earned a profit of $392,399.15 on all other Government business
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same distinctive accounting move: isolate the claimed loss, then compare it with profits across the contractor's larger body of government work.

shared_material.child_excerpt: it would be inequitable to grant relief to the Company with respect to the seven contracts on which it sustained losses, without giving consideration to the twenty-eight on which it made profits.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: My approval of this bill would establish the undesirable principle of Government underwriting any wartime losses incurred by contractors providing goods and services to the Government, regardless of the fact that such contractors did not sustain a net loss.
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts C18's substantive rationale that the Government should not compensate selected contract losses when the contractor was profitable overall.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The granting of relief in this case would also be discriminatory against many other contractors who sustained losses under fixed price contracts during the early part of the Korean War.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am unable to perceive any circumstances which would warrant preferential treatment for the claimant to the detriment of other wartime contractors.
shared_material.explanation: Both close by framing special relief as preferential or discriminatory treatment relative to other wartime government contractors.
